What Size Power Station Do I Need in Kenya?

Add up your watts, decide how many hours you need, and pick a capacity. Worked examples with live prices.

Last reviewed 9 November 2026 · Prices update automatically from our catalogue.

The short answer

Add up the watts of everything you want to keep running during a KPLC outage, multiply by the hours you need, and divide by 0.85 to allow for inverter losses. That gives the capacity, in watt-hours (Wh), to look for. Then check that the power station's AC output, in watts (W), is higher than everything you will run at the same time. Most Kenyan homes land between 1,000 Wh and 3,000 Wh.

Step 1: list your appliances and their watts

Every appliance has a power rating on its label or charger. If you cannot find it, these typical figures are a fair starting point — but the label on your own appliance always wins.

ApplianceTypical watts
LED bulb10 W
Phone charging10 W
Wi-Fi router15 W
TV decoder20 W
CCTV kit (4 cameras + recorder)40 W
Standing fan50 W
Laptop60 W
TV (43-inch LED)100 W
Fridge (running)150 W
Chest freezer (running)200 W
Microwave1,000 W
Electric kettle2,000 W

A fridge or freezer only draws its running watts part of the time, because the compressor switches on and off, so real use over a day is usually lower than the figure above. Heating appliances — kettles, irons, cookers and water heaters — draw a lot of power; a power station can run them only if its AC output is high enough, and they drain the battery quickly.

Step 2: decide how many hours you need

Think about your usual outages. A short evening blackout needs a few hours of backup; a full-day outage needs much more. Solar panels change the picture: if the power station recharges during the day, it only needs to carry you through the night.

Step 3: work out the capacity

Capacity (Wh) = total watts × hours ÷ 0.85. Here are three worked examples, each with the lowest-priced in-stock power station we sell that covers it today:

Apartment

Running Wi-Fi router, 4 LED bulbs, a TV and a laptop — about 215 W — for 4 hours needs 215 × 4 ÷ 0.85 ≈ 1,050 Wh. The BLUETTI AC180P (1,440 Wh, KES 67,000) covers it.

Family home

Running a fridge, Wi-Fi router, a TV, 6 LED bulbs and a decoder — about 345 W — for 6 hours needs 345 × 6 ÷ 0.85 ≈ 2,450 Wh. The BLUETTI Homestar 3 Solution (3,000 Wh, KES 111,500) covers it.

Whole home

Running a fridge, a chest freezer, Wi-Fi, two TVs, 10 LED bulbs, a fan and CCTV — about 755 W — for 8 hours needs 755 × 8 ÷ 0.85 ≈ 7,150 Wh. The BLUETTI EP2000 Solution (10kW Inverter + 14.6kWh Battery) (14,600 Wh, KES 762,700) covers it.

Step 4: check the AC output and surge

Capacity is how long; AC output is how much at once. Add up everything you will switch on together and make sure it is below the station's AC output. Motors in fridges, freezers and pumps briefly draw several times their running watts when they start, which is what the surge figure on each product page is for. If you plan to use a microwave or kettle, choose a station whose AC output comfortably exceeds that appliance's rating.

Step 5: plan how you will recharge

Every power station recharges from a wall socket when KPLC power is back. Most also accept solar panels, listed as the solar input on each product page; panels whose combined watts fit within that input will recharge it during the day. See our solar generator pairings for matched station-and-panel examples, or browse all solar panels.

Step 6: leave room to grow

Many power stations accept extra batteries, shown as "Expandable to" in their specifications, so you can start smaller and add capacity later. We stock 9 extra batteries from KES 27,949; check which model each one fits.

Quick size guide

Apartment or bedsitter (about 250–1,200 Wh): Wi-Fi, phones, a laptop, lights and a TV. Options from KES 30,500: BLUETTI Premium 30 V2, BLUETTI AC50P and EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus.

Family home (about 1,200–3,000 Wh): lights, Wi-Fi, a TV and a fridge through longer outages. Options from KES 67,000: BLUETTI AC180P, EcoFlow DELTA 3 2000 Air (EFD3A2000-UK) and BLUETTI Premium 200 V2.

Whole home (3,000 Wh and up): most of the house, including bigger appliances within the AC output. Options from KES 111,500: BLUETTI Homestar 3 Solution, BLUETTI Homestar 5 Solution and EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra.
